result.target_topic: Netlist patent infringement litigation (Texas and Germany)
result.target_summary: Netlist filed multiple patent infringement complaints in U.S. and German courts alleging infringement of various patents by Micron's memory modules and HBM products, seeking injunctive relief, damages, and fees.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures describe the specific patent infringement complaints filed by Netlist against Micron entities in U.S. (Western District of Texas and Dusseldorf) courts regarding memory modules (NVDIMMs, LRDIMMs) and seeking injunctive relief and damages. The 2023 and 2024 filings cite the same initial complaints from April 2021 and March 2022.

The 2023 disclosure D075 describes the filing of the E.D. Tex. complaints (June 2022) alleging infringement by memory modules and HBM products. The 2024 disclosure D063 details the verdict in that same E.D. Tex. litigation, where a jury found Micron liable for infringing patents via those memory modules. They share the specific subject of the Netlist E.D. Tex. litigation regarding memory modules.

previous_disclosures.summary: Netlist filed multiple patent infringement complaints against Micron entities in U.S. and German courts alleging infringement of patents related to non-volatile dual in-line memory modules, load-reduced dual in-line memory modules (LRDIMMs), memory modules, and HBM products, seeking injunctive relief and damages across these jurisdictions.

current_disclosures.summary: Netlist filed multiple patent infringement complaints in U.S. and German courts alleging infringement of various patents by Micron's memory modules and HBM products, seeking injunctive relief, damages, and fees.

In Netlist's E.D. Tex. litigation, a jury found Micron liable for infringing two patents, awarding $425 million and $20 million in damages, respectively; Micron intends to appeal, though the PTAB found the asserted claims unpatentable.

comparisons.peer_topic: Overview of Legal, Tax, and Environmental Contingencies
comparisons.peer_summary: The Company is involved in various legal actions, tax claims, and environmental matters in the normal course of business, including government clean-up activities at current or past locations.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Micron disclose general contingencies involving legal actions in the normal course of business. However, AMD's disclosure is broad and generic, mentioning various legal actions, tax claims, and environmental matters without detailing specific patent infringement cases, whereas Micron specifically details the Netlist patent infringement litigation across U.S. and German courts regarding memory products.

sentences.text: On April 28, 2021, Netlist, Inc. ("Netlist") filed two patent infringement actions against Micron, Micron Semiconductor Products, Inc. ("MSP"), and Micron Technology Texas, LLC ("MTEC") in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Texas.
The first complaint alleges that one U.S. patent is infringed by certain of our non-volatile dual in-line memory modules.
The second complaint alleges that three U.S. patents are infringed by certain of our load-reduced dual in-line memory modules ("LRDIMMs").
Each complaint seeks injunctive relief, damages, attorneys' fees, and costs.

On March 31, 2022, Netlist filed a patent infringement complaint against Micron and Micron Semiconductor Germany, GmbH in Dusseldorf Regional Court alleging that two German patents are infringed by certain of our LRDIMMs. The complaint seeks damages, costs, and injunctive relief.
From time to time the Company is a defendant or plaintiff in various legal actions that arise in the normal course of business.
The Company is also subject to income tax, indirect tax or other tax claims by tax agencies in jurisdictions in which it conducts business.

In addition, the Company is a party to environmental matters including local, regional, state and federal government clean-up activities at or near locations where the Company currently or has in the past conducted business.

In May 2024, R2 filed suit in Milan against Intel Corporation Italia S.P.A. and Italian affiliates of customers Dell, HP, and HPE, accusing Intel's Ice Lake (server and client), Tiger Lake, Alder Lake, and Raptor Lake processors of infringing its patent, and requesting that its suit be consolidated with Intel Corporation Italia S.P.A.'s suit.
In April 2024, R2 filed an action against Intel and its customers Dell, HP, and HPE for patent infringement before the Tribunal Judiciaire of Paris.

The plaintiffs in the putative securities class action lawsuit, captioned 4:18-cv-07669-HSG, initially filed on December 21, 2018 in the United States District Court for the Northern District of California, and titled In Re NVIDIA Corporation Securities Litigation, filed an amended complaint on May 13, 2020.

Plaintiffs sought class certification, an award of unspecified compensatory damages, an award of reasonable costs and expenses, including attorneys' fees and expert fees, and further relief as the Court may deem just and proper.
On March 30, 2021, plaintiffs filed an appeal from judgment in the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit, case number 21-15604.

On November 15, 2023, the Ninth Circuit denied NVIDIA's petition for rehearing en banc of the Ninth Circuit panel's majority decision to reverse in part the dismissal of the case, which NVIDIA had filed on October 10, 2023.

On November 21, 2023, NVIDIA filed a motion with the Ninth Circuit for a stay of the mandate pending NVIDIA's petition for a writ of certiorari in the Supreme Court of the United States and the Supreme Court's resolution of the matter.
